name: Sinasina Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language; only Rarrick archive deposit listed; no word-stress description applicable/found

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. 2025. Bridging Signed Language Documentation & Spoken Language Documentation. Language Documentation & Conservation 19: 24-39. hdl:10125/74809
sources.note: Methods article; nothing SSSL-specific on prosody. General remark (p. ~31) that eyeblinks 'play an important role in sign language prosody (Muir & Richardson 2005; Sze 2008; Pfau 2016)' and that non-manual head/face movements are often grammatical (Schembri 2010).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page sina1273 (Hammarström et al.) and reference record 584885 (Rarrick 2020)
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive references for sina1273 (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0); Rarrick 2020 is typed hhtype=socling and cited only for subclassification.

No linguistic description; reference list only: Rarrick 2019 ICLDC 'Training Signers to Document SSSL' (audio on ScholarSpace hdl:10125/44862), Rarrick 2019 LSA talk, Rarrick & Asonye 2017 ICLDC poster (hdl:10125/42056), Rarrick 2019 FEL XXIII talk.

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. 2024. Tok Pisin metalanguage: why is Sinasina Sign Language not tok ('language')? Language Sciences 102: 101611. doi:10.1016/j.langsci.2023.101611 (CC-BY; Griffith Research Online hdl:10072/427970)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/metalinguistic study of the Tok Pisin word tok and language ideologies around SSSL. The only 'phonological' mention concerns spoken-language cues used to recognise group membership (p. ~11).

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. 2021. Is Sinasina Sign Language an Isolate? A call for further sign language documentation & description in Papua New Guinea. Talk (slides + transcript), 7th International Conference on Language Documentation and Conservation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa, 5 March 2021. hdl:10125/74510
sources.note: Nothing on stress/prominence. Reports a lexicostatistic comparison of 'phonological parameters of core vocabulary' with PNGSL and the Enga (Lagaip) sign language (<50% shared), basic word order SOV, V+Neg, N+Adj, N+Num, SOV+Q, and non-manual markers: durative aspect = lip rounding, questions = eyebrow furrowing + lip rounding, negation = headshake (pp. 6-7 of transcript).

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. 2020. Sinasina Sign Language (Chimbu, Papua New Guinea) – Language Snapshot. Language Documentation and Description 19: 79-86. London: EL Publishing. doi:10.25894/ldd66
sources.note: Nothing. Sections: 1 Overview (signers, vitality, name), 1.1 Current and past signers, 1.2 Vitality, 1.3 label, 2 Current research. Only grammatical remark (p. 80): 'Word order in SSSL is frequently Subject-Object-Verb, but topic-comment structures are common in narratives.' p. 84 says a trilingual dictionary and 'sketch grammar' are in preparation. Zero hits for stress/accent/prosody/phonology.

sources.citation: Reed, Lauren W. 2019. Sign Languages of Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea, and their Challenges for Sign Language Typology. MA thesis, ANU (hdl 1885/165444)
sources.note: Nothing on SSSL beyond noting that Kailge signers watched Rarrick's videos of Sinasina signers and recognised some signs (c. p. 110) and listing Rarrick's 2017-2019 talks in the references.

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. In preparation (announced 2020). Sketch grammar of Sinasina Sign Language (with SSSL-Tok Pisin-English trilingual dictionary).
